outputs.L1:
The present invention relates to a heat exchanger capable of enhancing thermal efficiency by enabling combustion heat from combustion gas generated by combustion in a burner to be maximally transferred to a heating medium. The heat exchanger is provided with a heat exchange unit in which heating medium flow channels, through which a heating medium flows, and combustion gas flow channels, through which combustion gas combusted in the burner flows, are alternately formed adjacent to one another in spaces between a plurality of plates.

The heat exchange unit comprises: a sensible heat unit that surrounds the outer side of a combustion chamber, is formed in one side area of the plates, and heats the heating medium by using sensible heat of combustion gas generated by combustion in the burner; and a latent heat unit that is formed in the other side area of the plates and heats the heating medium by using latent heat of water vapor contained in combustion gas that has completed heat exchange in the sensible heat unit.

A flow channel cap is coupled to the rear of the sensible heat unit to provide a flow channel for the combustion gas, thereby enabling combustion gas that has passed through the combustion gas flow channels formed in the upper part of the sensible heat unit to enter the combustion gas flow channels of the latent heat unit.
outputs.L2:
The invention concerns a heat exchanger designed to improve thermal efficiency by allowing as much combustion heat as possible, from combustion gas produced by a burner, to be transferred back to a heating medium. The heat exchanger includes a heat exchange unit in which heating-medium flow passages, through which the heating medium moves, and combustion-gas flow passages, through which gas burned by the burner moves, are arranged alternately next to one another in the spaces between multiple plates.

The heat exchange unit includes a sensible heat section and a latent heat section. The sensible heat section is positioned around the outside of a combustion chamber, is made from one side region of the plates, and warms the heating medium using sensible heat from the combustion gas generated by burner combustion. The latent heat section is made from the other side region of the plates and warms the heating medium using latent heat from water vapor contained in the combustion gas after that gas has completed heat exchange in the sensible heat section.

A flow-channel cap is attached to the rear side of the sensible heat section to define a passage for the combustion gas, so that combustion gas exiting the combustion-gas flow passages formed in the upper portion of the sensible heat section can be guided into the combustion-gas flow passages of the latent heat section.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a heat exchanger designed to improve thermal efficiency by maximizing the amount of combustion heat returned to a heating medium, such as water. By effectively recovering both sensible heat and latent heat from combustion gas, the heat exchanger enables more efficient use of energy produced during combustion.

The heat exchanger is formed with multiple plates arranged to define alternating adjacent flow channels. These channels include flow paths for the heating medium and separate flow paths for combustion gas. By placing the heating medium channels next to the combustion gas channels, heat can be transferred efficiently through the plates from the hot combustion gas to the heating medium as the two fluids pass through the heat exchanger.

The heat exchanger includes a sensible heat unit positioned around a combustion chamber. This sensible heat unit receives high-temperature combustion gas generated by a burner and transfers the sensible heat of the gas to the heating medium. As the combustion gas flows through the sensible heat unit, its temperature is reduced while the heating medium absorbs heat and increases in temperature.

After passing through the sensible heat unit, the combustion gas is directed to a latent heat unit. The latent heat unit is configured to recover latent heat contained in water vapor within the combustion gas. As the combustion gas is further cooled in the latent heat unit, water vapor condenses, releasing latent heat that is also transferred to the heating medium. This additional heat recovery further improves the overall thermal efficiency of the heat exchanger.

A flow channel cap is coupled to the rear portion of the sensible heat unit. The flow channel cap functions to guide or redirect the combustion gas discharged from the sensible heat unit into the latent heat unit. By providing a controlled passage between the sensible heat unit and the latent heat unit, the flow channel cap helps ensure smooth gas flow and effective heat recovery throughout the heat exchanger.

Through this structure, the heat exchanger can recover a large portion of the heat generated by combustion, including both sensible heat and latent heat, thereby improving heating performance and reducing energy loss.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a heat exchanger designed to improve thermal efficiency by effectively recovering heat from combustion gas and transferring it to a heating medium, such as water. The heat exchanger is constructed by arranging a plurality of plates so that heating-medium flow channels and combustion-gas flow channels are formed alternately between adjacent plates. Through this plate-type structure, a large heat-transfer area is obtained, allowing heat from high-temperature combustion gas to be efficiently transmitted to the heating medium flowing through neighboring channels.

The heat exchanger includes two main heat-recovery sections: a sensible-heat unit and a latent-heat unit. In the sensible-heat unit, high-temperature combustion gas produced by a burner or combustion device first exchanges heat with the heating medium. This section primarily recovers sensible heat, that is, the heat associated with the temperature of the combustion gas itself. As the combustion gas passes through the sensible-heat unit, its temperature is reduced while the heating medium is heated.

After passing through the sensible-heat unit, the combustion gas is not discharged immediately. Instead, it is guided to the latent-heat unit through a rear flow-channel cap provided at the rear side of the heat exchanger. This rear flow-channel cap forms a passage that directs the combustion gas from the outlet side of the sensible-heat unit into the inlet side of the latent-heat unit. As a result, the flow of combustion gas is smoothly redirected and supplied to the latent-heat unit without the need for a complicated external duct structure.

In the latent-heat unit, the combustion gas is further cooled. When the temperature of the combustion gas falls below the dew point, water vapor contained in the gas condenses. During this condensation process, latent heat of vaporization is released. The latent-heat unit is configured to recover this latent heat and transfer it to the heating medium flowing through adjacent heating-medium channels. In this way, not only the sensible heat of the combustion gas but also the latent heat contained in water vapor can be effectively utilized.

Because the heating-medium channels and the combustion-gas channels are alternately arranged between plates in both the sensible-heat unit and the latent-heat unit, heat transfer is performed efficiently in a compact structure. The separate arrangement of the sensible-heat and latent-heat units also allows each section to be optimized according to the temperature and condensation conditions of the combustion gas. The sensible-heat unit can be designed to withstand higher temperatures, while the latent-heat unit can be configured to handle condensate generated during recovery of latent heat.

A key feature of the invention is the use of the rear flow-channel cap to guide the combustion gas from the sensible-heat unit into the latent-heat unit. This structure enables a continuous combustion-gas flow path through both heat-recovery sections and ensures that the residual heat remaining after sensible-heat recovery is further utilized in the latent-heat unit. Consequently, the overall heat recovery rate is increased, exhaust heat loss is reduced, and the thermal efficiency of the apparatus is improved.

Thus, the invention provides a compact and efficient heat exchanger capable of recovering both sensible heat and water-vapor latent heat from combustion gas. By transferring this recovered heat to the heating medium, the heat exchanger can reduce fuel consumption, improve energy efficiency, and enhance the performance of heating equipment such as boilers, water heaters, and similar combustion-based systems.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, but it plays an important role in how we communicate. It is called the definite article, and it helps point to something specific. For example, saying “a book” could mean any book, but saying “the book” tells us that we are talking about a particular one.

Although “the” is simple, it gives clarity and direction to a sentence. It helps readers and listeners understand exactly what is being discussed. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or unclear. Phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” and “the future” feel familiar because “the” connects us to shared ideas and specific meanings.

In everyday language, “the” is often unnoticed because it appears so frequently. However, its importance should not be underestimated. It is a small word with a big purpose: to make language more precise, natural, and meaningful.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing a heat exchanger with alternating heating medium and combustion gas channels, including a sensible heat unit around a combustion chamber, a latent heat unit, and a rear flow channel cap connecting the gas flow paths.
counterfactuals.output: A heat exchanger for a combustion apparatus is disclosed. The heat exchanger includes a sensible heat exchange unit disposed around at least a portion of a combustion chamber and defining a plurality of first heat-transfer flow channels through which a heating medium flows and a plurality of first combustion-gas flow channels through which combustion gas from the combustion chamber flows, the first heat-transfer flow channels and the first combustion-gas flow channels being alternately arranged to exchange sensible heat. A latent heat exchange unit is disposed downstream of the sensible heat exchange unit and defines a plurality of second heat-transfer flow channels and a plurality of second combustion-gas flow channels alternately arranged to recover latent heat from the combustion gas. A rear flow-channel cap is coupled to rear end portions of the sensible heat exchange unit and the latent heat exchange unit and defines a communication passage configured to guide combustion gas discharged from the first combustion-gas flow channels into the second combustion-gas flow channels. Accordingly, combustion heat is efficiently transferred to the heating medium while providing a compact flow-path structure and improved heat recovery efficiency.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft the “present invention relates to” section for a condensing boiler heat exchanger that maximizes return of combustion heat to a heating medium, where a sensible heat unit surrounds the combustion chamber and a latent heat unit recovers heat from water vapor in the exhaust gas.
counterfactuals.output: The present invention relates to a condensing boiler heat exchanger configured to maximize the recovery and transfer of combustion heat to a heating medium. More particularly, the present invention relates to a heat exchanger for a condensing boiler in which a sensible heat exchange unit is disposed to surround a combustion chamber so as to absorb sensible heat generated by combustion, and a latent heat exchange unit is arranged to recover latent heat from water vapor contained in exhaust gas discharged after combustion. counterfactuals.prompt: Create a technical patent paragraph explaining a plate-type heat exchanger for a burner, in which combustion gas and heating water flow through adjacent alternating channels, and a rear cap redirects gas from the sensible heat portion into the latent heat portion.
counterfactuals.output: A plate-type heat exchanger for a burner comprises a stacked plurality of heat-transfer plates joined to define alternating first and second flow channels arranged in adjacent heat-exchange relationship, wherein combustion gas generated by the burner flows through the first flow channels and heating water flows through the second flow channels in a counter-flow or cross-flow configuration. The heat exchanger includes a sensible-heat recovery portion disposed upstream with respect to a combustion-gas flow direction and a latent-heat recovery portion disposed downstream thereof, the sensible-heat recovery portion being configured to transfer heat from high-temperature combustion gas to the heating water, and the latent-heat recovery portion being configured to condense water vapor contained in the combustion gas and recover latent heat of condensation. A rear cap is coupled to a rear side of the stacked plates and defines a gas turnaround chamber communicating with outlets of the combustion-gas channels in the sensible-heat recovery portion and inlets of the combustion-gas channels in the latent-heat recovery portion, such that combustion gas discharged from the sensible-heat recovery portion is redirected by the rear cap and introduced into the latent-heat recovery portion. The rear cap thereby provides a compact gas-flow reversal path while maintaining separation between the combustion-gas channels and the heating-water channels, enabling improved thermal efficiency and reduced overall size of the burner heat exchanger.
